categories.label: Data & Research
categories.blurb: Original empirical and data-driven research into antizionist rhetoric, belief, and media coverage.

categories.label: Essays & Commentary
categories.blurb: Analysis and opinion writing on antizionism as ideology and political culture.

categories.label: Substacks
categories.blurb: Independent newsletters covering antizionism, antisemitism, and Jewish identity.

resources.title: At the Mind's Limits: Contemplations by a Survivor on Auschwitz and its Realities
resources.description: A Holocaust survivor's autobiographical account, which also includes a reckoning with postwar antizionism.
resources.reference: Améry, Jean. At the Mind's Limits. 1966.
resources.author: Jean Améry

resources.title: Essays on Antisemitism, Anti-Zionism, and the Left
resources.description: A posthumous English-language collection gathering Jean Améry's essays confronting antisemitism and antizionism, including his writings on the political currents of the postwar European left.
resources.reference: Améry, Jean. Essays on Antisemitism, Anti-Zionism, and the Left. Edited by Marlene Gallner. Translated by Louise Fischer. Indiana University Press, 2021.
resources.author: Jean Améry

resources.title: The Antizionist Complex
resources.description: One of the first book-length arguments that postwar hostility to Israel is a continuation of Judeophobia in a new guise; argues that opposition to Jewish national existence, however framed, ultimately derives from a refusal to accept a Jewish nation.
resources.reference: Givet, Jacques. The Antizionist Complex. SBS Publishing, 1979.
resources.author: Jacques Givet

resources.title: The History of Anti-Semitism
resources.description: A landmark four-volume history tracing Jew-hatred from antiquity through the rise of Nazism; the final volumes ("From Voltaire to Wagner," "Suicidal Europe") trace the emergence of racial antisemitism and end with Poliakov's own prescient warning that hatred of Jews might take on a new "anti-Zionist" guise.
resources.reference: Poliakov, Leon. The History of Anti-Semitism (multiple vols.). 1965–1977.
resources.author: Leon Poliakov

resources.title: The New Judeophobia
resources.description: Argues that a "new Judeophobia" emerged around the 2001 Durban conference, distinct from older racial antisemitism: it diabolizes Israel and Zionism (and by extension Jews) using antiracist and anti-imperialist language rather than racial theory.
resources.reference: Taguieff, Pierre-André. The New Judeophobia. 2002.
resources.author: Pierre-André Taguieff

resources.title: Judeophobia: The Last Wave
resources.description: Continues Taguieff's study of the mutations of Judeophobia, extending his analysis of 'anti-Zionist antisemitism' into its most recent, post-2000s forms.
resources.reference: Taguieff, Pierre-André. Judeophobia: The Last Wave. 2018.
resources.author: Pierre-André Taguieff

resources.title: The Left against Zion: Communism, Israel, and the Middle East
resources.description: An edited volume examining the Soviet bloc's turn against Israel after 1967 and the antisemitic character much of that "anti-Zionist" campaign took on.
resources.reference: Wistrich, Robert S. (ed.). The Left against Zion. Vallentine, Mitchell, 1979.
resources.author: Robert S. Wistrich (ed.)

resources.title: From Ambivalence to Betrayal: The Left, the Jews, and Israel (essay)
resources.description: Traces the European left's shift from ambivalence toward, to eventual hostility against, Jewish nationalism, foreshadowing Wistrich's larger 2012 book of a similar title.
resources.reference: Wistrich, Robert S. "From Ambivalence to Betrayal: The Left, the Jews, and Israel." In Anti-Zionism and Antisemitism in the Contemporary World, 2009.
resources.author: Robert S. Wistrich

resources.title: A Lethal Obsession
resources.description: A sweeping single-volume history of antisemitism "from antiquity to the global jihad," ending with chapters connecting the Soviet war on Zionism and contemporary jihadist and left-wing antisemitism to older Judeophobic traditions.
resources.reference: Wistrich, Robert S. A Lethal Obsession. Random House, 2010.
resources.author: Robert S. Wistrich

resources.title: The Jews in the Soviet Union Since 1917: Paradox of Survival
resources.description: A detailed two-volume history of Soviet Jewry, including the state's campaigns against Zionism and Hebrew culture from the 1920s onward.
resources.reference: Levin, Nora. The Jews in the Soviet Union Since 1917: Paradox of Survival. NYU Press, 1988.
resources.author: Nora Levin

resources.title: Contemporary Left Antisemitism
resources.description: Analyzes how antisemitism that goes unacknowledged in left-wing and liberal spaces (unions, academia, campaigns to boycott Israel) can hide behind the language of anti-imperialism and human rights; introduces Hirsh's concept of the "Livingstone Formulation," in which raising antisemitism is dismissed as a bad-faith attempt to silence criticism of Israel.
resources.reference: Hirsh, David. Contemporary Left Antisemitism. Routledge, 2017.
resources.author: David Hirsh

resources.title: From Antizionism to a New Middle East
resources.description: A collection of nine essays offering historical analysis, contemporary commentary, and practical solutions for a path to a multi-national and multi-religious Middle East, free of the mendacious and destructive force of antizionism.
resources.reference: Kirschbaum-Shirazki, Olga. From Antizionism to a New Middle East. 2026.
resources.author: Olga Kirschbaum-Shirazki

resources.title: Accusation in a Mirror
resources.description: Examines "accusation in a mirror," the propaganda technique documented before the Rwandan genocide of accusing one's intended victims of the very crimes one plans to commit, and traces it through Holocaust inversion and Iranian rhetoric that accuses Israel of genocidal intent while calling for its destruction. Argues that courts should treat it as strong evidence of the "directness" required to prosecute incitement to genocide.
resources.reference: Marcus, Kenneth L. "Accusation in a Mirror." Loyola University Chicago Law Journal, Vol. 43, No. 2, 2012.
resources.author: Kenneth L. Marcus

resources.title: Anti-Zionism & Anti-Semitism
resources.description: From the book examining how the U.S. civil-rights framework (Title VI) can and should apply to campus antisemitism, including where anti-Israel activism shades into discrimination against Jewish students.
resources.reference: Marcus, Kenneth L. "Anti-Zionism & Anti-Semitism." In The Definition of Anti-Semitism, 146–190. Oxford University Press, 2015.
resources.author: Kenneth L. Marcus

resources.title: From Ambiguity to Accountability: The Case for a Legal Definition of Antisemitism in Academia
resources.description: Argues, using post–October 7 campus data, that universities should formally adopt the IHRA definition of antisemitism in their nondiscrimination policies to close the ambiguity around antizionism as a form of antisemitism and restore Title VI accountability.
resources.reference: Martin, Andrea J. "From Ambiguity to Accountability: The Case for a Legal Definition of Antisemitism in Academia." Pepperdine Law Review, 2025.
resources.author: Andrea J. Martin

resources.title: Hamas' October 7th Genocide: Legal Analysis and the Weaponisation of Reverse Accusations
resources.description: Argues under the Genocide Convention that Hamas's October 7 attack itself meets the legal definition of genocide, and examines how the reverse "genocide" accusation against Israel functions to deflect that recognition.
resources.reference: Shalev, Avraham Russell. "Hamas' October 7th Genocide: Legal Analysis and the Weaponisation of Reverse Accusations—A Study in Modern Genocide Recognition and Denial." Israel Law Review, Vol. 58, Special Issue 2–3, 2025.
resources.author: Avraham Russell Shalev

resources.title: The Genocide Libel: How the World Has Charged Israel with Genocide
resources.description: A Holocaust historian traces how genocide accusations against Israel, unlike those leveled at other states, have persisted throughout its existence, and argues the post-October 7 version deploys classic antisemitic tropes (blood libel, Nazi inversion, collective Jewish guilt).
resources.reference: Goda, Norman J. W. "The Genocide Libel: How the World Has Charged Israel with Genocide." ISCA Research Paper 2025-3, Institute for the Study of Contemporary Antisemitism, Indiana University, 2025.
resources.author: Norman J. W. Goda

resources.title: On Three Antizionisms
resources.description: Argues that "antizionism" is not one coherent ideology but three distinct ideological clusters that happen to share a label, and that treating them as one obscures more than it clarifies.
resources.reference: Mor, Shany. "On Three Antizionisms." Israel Studies, Vol. 24, No. 2, 2019.
resources.author: Shany Mor

resources.title: Demonization Blueprints: Soviet Conspiracist Antizionism in Contemporary Left-Wing Discourse
resources.description: Traces how Soviet-era "anti-Zionist" propaganda campaigns (1967–88) built a conspiracist, demonizing template for talking about Israel that Tabarovsky argues has been absorbed largely intact into today's left-wing discourse.
resources.reference: Tabarovsky, Izabella. "Demonization Blueprints: Soviet Conspiracist Antizionism in Contemporary Left-Wing Discourse." Journal of Contemporary Antisemitism, vol. 5, no. 1, 2022, pp. 1-20.
resources.author: Izabella Tabarovsky

resources.title: The Anti-Zionist Mythology of the Left
resources.description: A shorter companion piece to Wistrich's From Ambivalence to Betrayal, dissecting the intellectual myths (Zionism as racism, colonialism, imperialism) that underpin the contemporary left's hostility to Israel.
resources.reference: Wistrich, Robert S. "The Anti-Zionist Mythology of the Left." Israel Journal of Foreign Affairs, 9:2, 2015.
resources.author: Robert S. Wistrich

resources.title: American Antizionism
resources.description: A sociologist argues that post-October 7 antizionism in the U.S. is best understood not as an intellectual critique of Zionism but as a mass political and social movement, with roots traced back through Poliakov's own 1969 prediction of a coming "anti-Zionist" mutation of antisemitism.
resources.reference: Kelner, Shaul. "American Antizionism." Sources: A Journal of Jewish Ideas, Fall/Winter 2025.
resources.author: Shaul Kelner

resources.title: "Anti-Zionism" and "Antizionism"
resources.description: Subtitled "the anti-Jewish worldview behind anti-Israel obsessions," it argues antizionism functions as a self-contained worldview that constructs its own caricature of Israel and positions it as central to global oppression.
resources.reference: Hirsh, David. "'Anti-Zionism' and 'Antizionism'." Australia/Israel & Jewish Affairs Council.
resources.author: David Hirsh

resources.title: Defeating Antizionism
resources.description: By an anthropologist and founder of the Movement Against Antizionism (MAAZ), arguing antizionism should be named and fought as its own distinct hate ideology rather than folded into debates over "antisemitism."
resources.reference: Louis-Klein, Adam. "Defeating Antizionism." Sapir, Issue 12, 2026.
resources.author: Adam Louis-Klein

resources.title: What Antizionism Really Is
resources.description: Continues Louis-Klein's argument that antizionism is a structured ideology with its own libels (colonizer, apartheid, genocide) rather than simply a political stance on Israeli policy.
resources.reference: Louis-Klein, Adam. "What Antizionism Really Is." The Free Press.
resources.author: Adam Louis-Klein

resources.title: Rwanda, Israel and the Inversion of 'Genocide'
resources.description: Argues that today's genocide accusations against Israel by defenders of Hamas follow the same rhetorical playbook Hutu extremists used against Tutsis in Rwanda in 1993 — inverting the language of genocide to accuse the actual targets of it.
resources.reference: Louis-Klein, Adam. "Rwanda, Israel and the Inversion of 'Genocide.'" The Wall Street Journal, July 22, 2026.
resources.author: Adam Louis-Klein

resources.title: The Left-Wing Case Against Anti-Zionism
resources.description: Makes the case, aimed at a left-leaning audience, that opposing antizionism is consistent with — not opposed to — progressive values.
resources.reference: Louis-Klein, Adam. "The Left-Wing Case Against Anti-Zionism." The Atlantic.
resources.author: Adam Louis-Klein

resources.title: The Cult of Antizionism
resources.description: Examines the founding of an academic "Institute for the Critical Study of Zionism" as an attempt to revive the Soviet-era discipline of "scientific antizionism" within American universities.
resources.reference: Tabarovsky, Izabella. "The Cult of 'Antizionism.'" Tablet Magazine.
resources.author: Izabella Tabarovsky

resources.title: Zombie Antizionism
resources.description: Discussion of how Soviet-origin antizionist tropes, long assumed dead, keep resurfacing largely unchanged in Western left-wing discourse.
resources.reference: Tabarovsky, Izabella. "Zombie Antizionism." Tablet Magazine.
resources.author: Izabella Tabarovsky

resources.title: Soviet Antizionism and Contemporary Left Antisemitism
resources.description: Lays out how the USSR's Cold War-era antizionist propaganda apparatus supplied the conspiratorial vocabulary and imagery still used against Israel and Zionism today.
resources.reference: Tabarovsky, Izabella. "Soviet Antizionism and Contemporary Left Antisemitism." Fathom Journal.
resources.author: Izabella Tabarovsky

resources.title: Antizionism: Projection and Replacement Theology
resources.description: Argues that antizionism in its Soviet, progressive, Islamist, Nazi, Christian, and Enlightenment-liberal forms shares two structures: a projection onto Israel of whatever each group considers evil, and a "replacement theology" in which one culture or ideology claims to supersede Judaism and so sees no need to understand Jews on their own terms. Calls for exposing replacement theology in education alongside antizionist libels.
resources.reference: Kirschbaum-Shirazki, Olga. "Antizionism: Projection and Replacement Theology."
resources.author: Olga Kirschbaum-Shirazki

resources.title: They Don't Believe It Either
resources.description: A philosopher of science (known for work on belief, ideology and pseudoscience) argues that much of the post-October 7 "genocide" rhetoric aimed at Israel functions less as a sincerely held factual belief than as a performative, tribal signal.
resources.reference: Boudry, Maarten. "They Don't Believe It Either." Quillette, Oct. 19, 2025.
resources.author: Maarten Boudry

resources.title: The Shadow of Babi Yar: How the Soviets Taught the West to Erase the Jews
resources.description: Uses the Soviet-era suppression of the memory of the Babi Yar massacre as a case study for how erasing Jewish victimhood became a template later adopted by Western antizionist discourse.
resources.reference: Lekht, Naya. "The Shadow of Babi Yar: How the Soviets Taught the West to Erase the Jews." Jewish Journal.
resources.author: Naya Lekht

resources.title: Three Failed Strategies of Inward Advocacy
resources.description: Argues that Jewish communal advocacy has relied on three failed strategies of "inward advocacy" (self-promotion, aligning Israel with fashionable values, and correcting facts) that treat antizionist libels as misinformation and keep Jews in the defendant's seat. Calls for turning the lens on the accuser by exposing antizionism's Soviet origins and teaching ideological literacy.
resources.reference: Lekht, Naya. "Three Failed Strategies of Inward Advocacy." JNS.
resources.author: Naya Lekht

resources.title: Scaffolding Anti-Zionism: The Hate We Missed
resources.description: Argues that teaching antisemitism as generic intolerance and scapegoating has left people unable to recognize antizionism as the third, mutated form of Jew-hatred after anti-Judaism and antisemitism, one that constructs Jews as villains through libels such as "Zionism is racism." Calls for education that exposes antizionist libels as earlier generations exposed antisemitic ones.
resources.reference: Lekht, Naya. "Scaffolding Anti-Zionism: The Hate We Missed." Jewish Journal, 2025.
resources.author: Naya Lekht

resources.title: The Eternal Settler
resources.description: Written after a wave of antisemitic attacks in Montreal, argues that even the Diaspora's oldest and largest Jewish communities (not just Israelis) are increasingly branded "settlers" in antizionist rhetoric — a designation Wexler argues has no logical stopping point.
resources.reference: Wexler, Benjamin. "The Eternal Settler." K. (Les Juifs, l'Europe, le XXIe siècle), June 20, 2024.
resources.author: Benjamin Wexler

resources.title: The History of the Charge of Genocide Against Israel
resources.description: A two-part historical investigation tracing the "genocide" accusation against Israel back through the revival of Arab nationalism (1920s–40s) and its absorption of European fascist and antisemitic ideas, then showing how those ideological roots fed the settler-colonialism framework used to level the charge today.
resources.reference: Szeftel, Daniel. "The History of the Charge of Genocide Against Israel." K. (Part 1 and Part 2).
resources.author: Daniel Szeftel

resources.title: The Greatest Threat to Jewish Safety Has a New Name
resources.description: An Australian writer on politics and Jewish affairs argues that antizionism, rather than traditional far-right antisemitism, has become the primary vector of anti-Jewish hostility today.
resources.reference: Dabelstein, Joshua. "The Greatest Threat to Jewish Safety Has a New Name." Australian Financial Review.
resources.author: Joshua Dabelstein

resources.title: A Deep Historical Irony of Anti-Zionism: Lessons from Poland
resources.description: Draws on Poland's 1968 state-orchestrated "anti-Zionist" purge, in which the label "Zionist" functioned as a euphemism for "Jew" and drove out most of the country's remaining Jewish population all while antisemitism was illegal.
resources.reference: McCallum, Alasdair. "A Deep Historical Irony of Anti-Zionism: Lessons from Poland." The Jewish Independent.
resources.author: Alasdair McCallum

resources.title: I've Seen This Before
resources.description: Interactive data analysis on the overlap of Soviet anti-Zionist propaganda and today's antizionist speech.
resources.reference: "I've Seen This Before." Data analysis, mapping Soviet anti-Zionist propaganda to modern echoes using semantic similarity.

resources.title: Antizionism Is a Totalitarian Conspiracy Theory Rotting the West From Within
resources.description: Argues antizionism is not ordinary criticism of Israeli policy but a modernized, eliminationist hate ideology with its own closed analytical framework, comparable to other totalizing conspiracy theories.
resources.reference: Heath, Allister. "Antizionism Is a Totalitarian Conspiracy Theory Rotting the West From Within." The Telegraph.
resources.author: Allister Heath

resources.title: Antizionism Is Not Antisemitism
resources.description: Argues that treating antizionism as one species of "antisemitism" undersells it as its own freestanding ideology of Jew-hatred.
resources.reference: Kaufman, Rona. "Antizionism Is Not Antisemitism." The Times of Israel Blogs.
resources.author: Rona Kaufman

resources.title: The Court Is Wrong: Antizionism Is Discriminatory
resources.description: Argues that a specific court ruling wrongly treated antizionist conduct as protected political speech rather than as discriminatory conduct against Jewish people.
resources.reference: Kaufman, Rona. "The Court Is Wrong: Antizionism Is Discriminatory." The Times of Israel Blogs.
resources.author: Rona Kaufman

resources.title: The Antizionist Movement Is a Hate Movement: It's Time to Say So
resources.description: Written after the 2025 Bondi Beach Hanukkah attack in Australia, argues — using the Southern Poverty Law Center's own definition of an antisemitic hate group — that the antizionist movement now meets that standard.
resources.reference: Martin, Andrea J. "The Antizionist Movement Is a Hate Movement: It's Time to Say So." The Times of Israel Blogs.
resources.author: Andrea J. Martin

resources.title: When Courts Minimize Terrorism, Jewish Students Pay the Price
resources.description: Argues that courts downplaying pro-terror conduct on campus leaves Jewish students unprotected under civil-rights law.
resources.reference: Martin, Andrea J. "When Courts Minimize Terrorism, Jewish Students Pay the Price." The Times of Israel Blogs.
resources.author: Andrea J. Martin

resources.title: The BDS Pound of Flesh
resources.description: A former Israeli MK argues that BDS-style campaigns to publicly shame students into disavowing Israel are a deliberate strategy to raise the "psychic and professional cost" of being Jewish.
resources.reference: Wilf, Einat. "The BDS Pound of Flesh." Tablet Magazine.
resources.author: Einat Wilf

resources.title: Moral Inversion and the Rise of Authoritarian Sympathy
resources.description: A data study finding that antizionist views correlate with a broader "moral inversion" — a systematic tendency to misjudge or invert the actual human-rights records of authoritarian versus democratic states.
resources.reference: Dulberg, Zack, et al. Moral Inversion and the Rise of Authoritarian Sympathy. Rutgers University Social Perception Lab / Network Contagion Research Institute.
resources.author: Zack Dulberg et al.

resources.title: Anti-Judaism: The Western Tradition
resources.description: Argues that anti-Judaism is not a fringe extremism but a foundational conceptual tool of Western thought itself. Nirenberg shows that Jews have represented what societies tend to to define themselves against. He traces this paradigm from antiquity through the Enlightenment and just past the Holocaust.
resources.reference: Nirenberg, David. Anti-Judaism: The Western Tradition. W.W. Norton & Co., 2013.
resources.author: David Nirenberg

resources.title: The Final Solution to the Jewish Question: A Love Story for the Living
resources.description: A follow-up to Horn's People Love Dead Jews, drawing on her post-October 7 work advising Harvard, the White House, and Congress; diagnoses failures of Holocaust education and the long history of antizionism, and proposes a path forward.
resources.reference: Horn, Dara. The Final Solution to the Jewish Question: A Love Story for the Living. Simon & Schuster, 2026.
resources.author: Dara Horn

resources.title: Be a Refusenik: A Jewish Student's Survival Guide
resources.description: Pairs the stories of Soviet-era refuseniks — Jews who defied a state doctrine equating Zionism with racism and genocide — with those of Jewish students facing similar antizionist pressure on American campuses today, drawing practical strategies from the earlier movement. Foreword by Natan Sharansky.
resources.reference: Tabarovsky, Izabella. Be a Refusenik: A Jewish Student's Survival Guide. Wicked Son, 2025.
resources.author: Izabella Tabarovsky

resources.title: Movement Against Antizionism
resources.description: A non-partisan, emergency-response initiative confronting a rapidly escalating antizionist hate movement that is actively endangering Jewish communities worldwide.
resources.reference: Movement Against Antizionism. Movement Against Antizionism (Substack).
resources.author: Movement Against Antizionism

resources.title: Movement Against Antizionism AU
resources.description: Australian affiliate of the Movement Against Antizionism, headed by Joshua Dabelstein; grassroots training and education on antizionism.
resources.reference: Movement Against Antizionism Australia. Movement Against Antizionism AU (Substack).
resources.author: Movement Against Antizionism Australia

resources.title: Institute for the Critical Study of Antizionism
resources.description: To promote the critical study of the most current manifestation of the world's oldest hatred.
resources.reference: Pessin, Andrew. Institute for the Critical Study of Antizionism (Substack).
resources.author: Andrew Pessin

resources.title: Jennifer Kogan
resources.description: "Jewish Fierce Compassion": a clinical social worker analyzes antizionism through a psychological-abuse framework. Levari, offering trauma-informed education on antizionism, publishes here too.
resources.reference: Kogan, Jennifer. Jennifer Kogan (Substack).
resources.author: Jennifer Kogan

resources.title: Adam Louis-Klein
resources.description: Newsletter by the anthropologist and founder of the Movement Against Antizionism (MAAZ).
resources.reference: Louis-Klein, Adam. Adam Louis-Klein (Substack).
resources.author: Adam Louis-Klein

resources.title: Naya's Newsletter
resources.description: Politics, education, history, antisemitism, and Jewish identity.
resources.reference: Lekht, Naya. Naya's Newsletter (Substack).
resources.author: Naya Lekht

resources.title: Pariah--But The Truth, You Know, Ain't A Democracy
resources.description: Musings both non-fictional and fictional (it can sometimes be hard to tell the difference).
resources.reference: Pessin, Andrew. Pariah (Substack).
resources.author: Andrew Pessin

resources.title: The New Refuseniks
resources.description: Exploring themes from Tabarovsky's research and writing on Soviet and contemporary antizionism, Jewish identity, freedom, courage, and resistance.
resources.reference: Tabarovsky, Izabella. The New Refuseniks (Substack).
resources.author: Izabella Tabarovsky

resources.title: Einat Wilf
resources.description: Speaker and writer.
resources.reference: Wilf, Einat. Einat Wilf (Substack).
resources.author: Einat Wilf

resources.title: Beyond Belief
resources.description: Israel, the Middle East, and the politics, philosophy, and history that still burn beneath them.
resources.reference: Hyde, Samuel J. Beyond Belief (Substack).
resources.author: Samuel J. Hyde

resources.title: After October 7
resources.description: Original watchdog reporting on Jewish issues, helping readers make sense of the post-October 7 world.
resources.reference: Deutsch, Kevin. After October 7 (Substack).
resources.author: Kevin Deutsch

resources.title: COUNTERINTUITIVE
resources.description: Commentary by writer David Christopher Kaufman on antizionism, Jewish identity, and politics.
resources.reference: Kaufman, David Christopher. COUNTERINTUITIVE (Substack).
resources.author: David Christopher Kaufman

resources.title: For Normal People
resources.description: Reader-funded publication by Australian writer Joshua Dabelstein, combining political and cultural analysis, reviews, and philosophical meanderings.
resources.reference: Dabelstein, Joshua. For Normal People (Substack).
resources.author: Joshua Dabelstein

resources.title: Being Jewish with Jonah Platt
resources.description: Interviews on Jewish identity and antizionism from a mainstream, entertainment-adjacent angle.
resources.reference: Platt, Jonah. Being Jewish with Jonah Platt (Substack).
resources.author: Jonah Platt

resources.title: Sarah Ettedgui
resources.description: A Mizrahi/Sephardic lawyer writing on antizionism in society.
resources.reference: Ettedgui, Sarah. Sarah Ettedgui (Substack).
resources.author: Sarah Ettedgui

resources.title: Antizionism as a Distinct Anti-Jewish Bigotry
resources.description: Argues antizionism is a coherent ideology with its own genealogy (Nazi-Islamist axis, Soviet propaganda, Western settler-colonial theory) and a recurring triad of libels (colonizer, apartheid, genocide) — and that it inverts classical antisemitism: where the old hatred cast Jews as alien outsiders, antizionism denies Jewish peoplehood and indigeneity outright.
resources.reference: Louis-Klein, Adam. 'Antizionism as a Distinct Anti-Jewish Bigotry.' Journal of Contemporary Antisemitism, Vol. 9, No. 1, 2026.
resources.author: Adam Louis-Klein

resources.title: On Antizionism and Unlearning Arab Supremacy
resources.description: Argues that much contemporary antizionism rests on unexamined assumptions of Arab political and cultural primacy in the Middle East, denying Jewish indigeneity and minimizing the historic persecution and displacement of Middle Eastern Jews. Calls for 'unlearning Arab supremacy' the same way other forms of ethnic or colonial privilege get critically examined.
resources.reference: Bacharach, Barak. 'On Antizionism and Unlearning Arab Supremacy.' Haverford College Political Science Department, Alumni Corner.
resources.author: Barak Bacharach

resources.title: March '68. Historical Facts
resources.description: The POLIN Museum's own historical account of the March 1968 crisis: a suppressed student rally that the Polish communist authorities turned into a state-run antisemitic campaign, forcing roughly 13,000 Polish Jews out of the country and ending organized Jewish life in Poland.
resources.reference: POLIN Museum of the History of Polish Jews. 'March '68. Historical Facts.'
resources.author: POLIN Museum of the History of Polish Jews

resources.title: 13,000 Jews Were Driven Out of Poland in 1968. Now, Some Are Returning to Tell Their Story.
resources.description: Follows Polish-Jewish emigrants of the 1968 antisemitic purge who returned to Poland decades later on an Engaged Memory Consortium trip, revisiting the state-run 'anti-Zionist' campaign that stripped them of jobs, schools, and citizenship, and reckoning with how little-known this history remains today.
resources.reference: Bartov, Shira Li. '13,000 Jews Were Driven Out of Poland in 1968. Now, Some Are Returning to Tell Their Story.' SA Jewish Report (via JTA), June 15, 2026.
resources.author: Shira Li Bartov

resources.title: The 1968 Forced Exodus of Polish Jewry on Film
resources.description: Surveys how Polish filmmakers have documented and interpreted the 1968 'March emigration' on screen, from Marian Marzyński's own exile documentary Skibet/Hatikvah through later films grappling with Polish-Jewish identity and the anti-Zionist purge that provoked it.
resources.reference: Shpolberg, Masha. 'The 1968 Forced Exodus of Polish Jewry on Film.' Tablet Magazine, May 1, 2018.
resources.author: Masha Shpolberg

resources.title: Center of Attention: Why One of the World's Tiniest Countries Gets the Biggest International Spotlight
resources.description: Argues Israel receives 7 to 600 times more international news coverage per capita than comparable countries, regardless of active conflict, and traces that disparity to a deliberate, decades-long influence campaign rooted in Soviet-era intelligence operations and sustained by later institutional and funding networks; draws on the author's GDELT-based media-coverage dataset (see companion methodology piece).
resources.reference: Musighi, Jeremy. "Center of Attention: Why One of the World's Tiniest Countries Gets the Biggest International Spotlight." profoundAF, Aug. 27, 2026.
resources.author: Jeremy Musighi

resources.title: Where the Soviets Won
resources.description: Argues that Soviet state antizionism collapsed with the USSR because the Soviet intelligentsia recognized it as official propaganda, while in the West the same educated class embraced it voluntarily after it arrived in the 1960s–70s attached to the language of antiracism. Calls for reforming American education so that antisemitism is no longer taught only as a form of racial hatred.
resources.reference: Lekht, Naya. "Where the Soviets Won." Sapir, Volume 22, Summer 2026.
resources.author: Naya Lekht

resources.title: How Antizionism’s Libels Against Israel Mirror the Prelude to the Rwandan Genocide
resources.description: The author summarizes a Wall Street Journal essay by Adam Louis-Klein arguing that accusations of genocide against Israel parallel Hutu propaganda that falsely accused Tutsis of genocide before 1994. It contends that the 'settler-colonial' framing mirrors colonial-era 'Hamitic' racial myths and calls for exposing this pattern while still permitting critique of specific Israeli policies.
resources.reference: Movement Against Antizionism. "How Antizionism’s Libels Against Israel Mirror the Prelude to the Rwandan Genocide." Substack, July 23, 2026.
resources.author: Movement Against Antizionism

resources.title: How to Punish a "Zionist"
resources.description: Using sarcasm, the author walks through the core antizionist claims (whiteness, settler-colonialism, supremacy, apartheid, genocide) and rebuts each by pointing to historical facts, Soviet and UN origins, and antisemitic precedents. The author concludes that antizionism functions as classical antisemitism with a record of harm to Jewish communities.
resources.reference: Movement Against Antizionism. "How to Punish a "Zionist"." Substack, June 28, 2026.
resources.author: Movement Against Antizionism

resources.title: This Essay Has No Right to Exist
resources.description: The author presents a lyrical, literary essay tracing antizionism as the latest form of ancient Jew-hatred, in which society projects its guilt onto Jews through libels like colonizer, genocide, and baby-killer. Citing recent attacks and figures from politics, media, and entertainment, the author argues that Jews must stop turning their gaze inward and instead name and confront antizionism directly.
resources.reference: Movement Against Antizionism. "This Essay Has No Right to Exist." Substack, June 3, 2026.
resources.author: Movement Against Antizionism

resources.title: End Antizionism Denial Now (Dispatch #14)
resources.description: The author argues that antizionism is a coherent, eliminationist hate movement and that widespread denial of this, from Jewish anti-Zionists, mainstream Jewish institutions, and political figures, enables it. He cites Iranian attacks and plots, the Beinart and Sanders statements, and examples of campus and cultural antizionism, and calls for naming antizionism plainly and confronting it.
resources.reference: Movement Against Antizionism. "End Antizionism Denial Now (Dispatch #14)." Substack, March 22, 2026.
resources.author: Movement Against Antizionism

resources.title: Meet the Architects of Academic Antizionism (Dispatch #13)
resources.description: The author traces a roughly century-long genealogy of antizionism in academia, from Soviet and Arab nationalist propaganda through postcolonial theory and settler-colonial theory to the construction of the genocide libel. The dispatch names key scholars at each stage and argues they embedded antizionist ideology in academic institutions, with several Jewish or Israeli-born figures tokenized for added legitimacy.
resources.reference: Movement Against Antizionism. "Meet the Architects of Academic Antizionism (Dispatch #13)." Substack, March 18, 2026.
resources.author: Movement Against Antizionism

resources.title: Antizionism Is Not Jewish Anti-Zionism (Dispatch #12)
resources.description: The author argues that conflating pre-1948 Jewish anti-Zionism, a set of intra-Jewish debates, with contemporary antizionism, which he characterizes as a hate ideology denying Jews the right to political self-determination, gives the latter cover and endangers Jewish communities. He urges hyphenation-based terminological precision, naming antizionism as hate, and asking non-Jews for help in interrupting it.
resources.reference: Movement Against Antizionism. "Antizionism Is Not Jewish Anti-Zionism (Dispatch #12)." Substack, March 13, 2026.
resources.author: Movement Against Antizionism

resources.title: Dispatch #11: Apartheid Week Is Coming. Are We Ready?
resources.description: The author argues that Israeli Apartheid Week and the apartheid charge against Israel derive from anti-Judaic theology, Arab nationalist and Soviet propaganda, and the 2001 Durban conference, and that the label is historically inaccurate, selectively applied, and used to justify boycotts and exclusion of Jews and Israelis. He calls for coordinated public, campus, and social media counter-campaigns ahead of this year's Apartheid Week.
resources.reference: Movement Against Antizionism. "Dispatch #11: Apartheid Week Is Coming. Are We Ready?." Substack, Feb. 12, 2026.
resources.author: Movement Against Antizionism

resources.title: Dispatch #10: How Jewish Discourse Misdiagnoses Antizionism
resources.description: The author argues that Jewish discourse repeatedly misdiagnoses antizionism through seven rhetorical habits, including 'cross the line' framing, the 'mask' metaphor, hyphenating 'anti-Zionism,' and claiming 'it's not about Israel.' He contends these habits fold antizionism into older forms of antisemitism rather than treating it as a distinct ideology aimed at eliminating Israel and purging those labeled 'Zionists,' and he proposes clearer language instead.
resources.reference: Movement Against Antizionism. "Dispatch #10: How Jewish Discourse Misdiagnoses Antizionism." Substack, Jan. 26, 2026.
resources.author: Movement Against Antizionism

resources.title: Dispatch #9: Why the Jewish World Is Unprepared for the U.S. Midterm Elections—and How to Fix It
resources.description: The author argues that antizionism is mainstreaming across the American left and increasingly the right, comparing current purges of Jews labeled "Zionists" to earlier MENA, Soviet, and Polish campaigns. He contends that antizionism remains invisible to the public and urges Jewish organizations to educate about it and press political candidates with a provided question list before the midterms.
resources.reference: Movement Against Antizionism. "Dispatch #9: Why the Jewish World Is Unprepared for the U.S. Midterm Elections—and How to Fix It." Substack, Dec. 29, 2025.
resources.author: Movement Against Antizionism

resources.title: Dispatch #8: Why Physical Self-Defense Is Not a Politics
resources.description: The author argues that the turn toward armed self-defense after the Bondi Hanukkah massacre reflects Jewish civic retreat, and that Jewish organizations have failed for decades to name antizionism as the ideology driving anti-Jewish hate. He contends antizionism is a libel-narrative system with Nazi-Arab, Soviet, and settler-colonial roots that operates across left and right, and calls for precise public campaigns against it.
resources.reference: Movement Against Antizionism. "Dispatch #8: Why Physical Self-Defense Is Not a Politics." Substack, Dec. 22, 2025.
resources.author: Movement Against Antizionism

resources.title: Dispatch #7: How the ADL’s Messaging Guidelines Undermine Jewish Self-Defense
resources.description: The author argues that the ADL's 2024 messaging guidelines, which discourage using the word antizionism and emphasize Jewish relatability and ally messengers, undermine Jewish self-defense. He proposes the MAAZ framework of principles for speaking plainly, starting with naming antizionism as a distinct ideology separate from classical antisemitism and religious antijudaism.
resources.reference: Movement Against Antizionism. "Dispatch #7: How the ADL’s Messaging Guidelines Undermine Jewish Self-Defense." Substack, Dec. 14, 2025.
resources.author: Movement Against Antizionism

resources.title: Dispatch #6: The Political Rationalization of Anti-Jewish Hate
resources.description: The author argues that every era justifies anti-Jewish hatred as a political response to supposed Jewish offenses, tracing this from medieval libels through Dreyfus and Kristallnacht to the Amsterdam attacks and the Boulder firebombing. He contends that contemporary antizionist narratives (colonizer, apartheid, genocide) are libels in the same lineage, and that softening our language for them obscures the pattern.
resources.reference: Movement Against Antizionism. "Dispatch #6: The Political Rationalization of Anti-Jewish Hate." Substack, Dec. 8, 2025.
resources.author: Movement Against Antizionism

resources.title: Dispatch #4: Beyond Meteorological Discourse
resources.description: The author argues that Jewish responses to antizionism are stuck in defensive self-scrutiny and vague 'meteorological' language that hides perpetrators. He calls for a Jewish civil-rights consciousness with a precise vocabulary naming antizionist slurs, libels, conspiracies, exclusion, harassment and violence, and he examines why Jews resist naming antizionism.
resources.reference: Movement Against Antizionism. "Dispatch #4: Beyond Meteorological Discourse." Substack, Nov. 24, 2025.
resources.author: Movement Against Antizionism

resources.title: Dispatch #3: The Genealogy of Antizionist Hate
resources.description: The author traces antizionism from Lenin and the Yevsektsiya through Soviet propaganda, into Arab nationalism and expulsions of Jews from the Middle East, and then into Western academia and activism, culminating in its post-October 7 surge. The author argues it is a coherent ideology of exclusion that should be critically studied, and the post also includes a call for personal stories for a podcast series.
resources.reference: Movement Against Antizionism. "Dispatch #3: The Genealogy of Antizionist Hate." Substack, Nov. 17, 2025.
resources.author: Movement Against Antizionism

resources.title: Welcome to the Movement Against Antizionism (MAAZ)
resources.description: The author introduces the Movement Against Antizionism and, drawing on Naya Lekht's framework, argues that Jew-hatred has taken three forms: religious antijudaism, racial antisemitism, and nation-based antizionism. The post urges precise naming of antizionism, advises focusing on uncommitted audiences rather than committed ideologues, and offers calls to action and an upcoming CUNY lecture announcement.
resources.reference: Movement Against Antizionism. "Welcome to the Movement Against Antizionism (MAAZ)." Substack, Nov. 7, 2025.
resources.author: Movement Against Antizionism

resources.title: By Rebecca Nesvet: “Profiles and Cowardice: Anti-Zionism: A Jewish History and the New York Public Library”
resources.description: The author argues that Benjamin Moser's 'Anti-Zionism: A Jewish History' is riddled with hyperbole, misinformation, and disingenuous use of evidence, including profiles of subjects who are not clearly Jewish or who held contradictory views. The author also contends that the New York Public Library, which hosted Moser as a Cullman Fellow, has urgent questions to answer about the book.
resources.reference: Institute for Critical Study of Antizionism (ICSA). "By Rebecca Nesvet: “Profiles and Cowardice: Anti-Zionism: A Jewish History and the New York Public Library”." Substack, Oct. 4, 2026.
resources.author: Institute for Critical Study of Antizionism (ICSA)

resources.title: By Simon Lucas, “Morbus Israel—case notes on a discipline in exitus”
resources.description: The author argues, through satire, thought experiments, and case studies from bioethics and philosophy journals, that antizionism has corrupted editorial standards and moral reasoning in the discipline. He presents a ten-part diagnostic manual of rhetorical and scholarly pathologies and contends the field has become a vehicle for delegitimizing Israel and fostering antisemitic double standards.
resources.reference: Institute for Critical Study of Antizionism (ICSA). "By Simon Lucas, “Morbus Israel—case notes on a discipline in exitus”." Substack, Sept. 12, 2026.
resources.author: Institute for Critical Study of Antizionism (ICSA)

resources.title: By Jeffrey Malkan, "The Fall of Jewish Columbia"
resources.description: The author argues that Columbia University's faculty and students, driven by critical race theory and a settler-colonial worldview, have turned the campus against Jews and Israel, culminating in the 2024 encampments and celebration of October 7. He frames this as a betrayal of academic vocation, comparable to the treason of German intellectuals in the 1920s, and as a revival of Jewish scapegoating.
resources.reference: Institute for Critical Study of Antizionism (ICSA). "By Jeffrey Malkan, "The Fall of Jewish Columbia"." Substack, July 26, 2026.
resources.author: Institute for Critical Study of Antizionism (ICSA)

resources.title: By Jones and Gisle: "The Antizionist Script: How Two Strangers Reached the Same Conclusion"
resources.description: Two authors, Jones and Gisle, each recount how they came to antizionism through academia and punk/anarchist activism, and how October 7th led them away from it. They argue the movement uses an identical script of 'colonizer, apartheid, genocide', drawn from Said, Fanon, Wolfe and others, and that it shuts out dissenters and ultimately targets Jews.
resources.reference: Institute for Critical Study of Antizionism (ICSA). "By Jones and Gisle: "The Antizionist Script: How Two Strangers Reached the Same Conclusion"." Substack, July 15, 2026.
resources.author: Institute for Critical Study of Antizionism (ICSA)

resources.title: By Barry Finger, "Review of Molly Crabapple, 'Here Where We Live Is Our Country' (Random House, 2026)"
resources.description: The author reviews Molly Crabapple's book, which holds up the anti-Zionist Bund as a model for leftist Jews today, and argues she ignores Labor Zionism's critique of Bundism and the Bund's historical failures. He traces the socialist movement's indifference to Jewish survival and contends that both the Bund and Labor Zionists offered serious but competing programs for Jewish national survival.
resources.reference: Institute for Critical Study of Antizionism (ICSA). "By Barry Finger, "Review of Molly Crabapple, 'Here Where We Live Is Our Country' (Random House, 2026)"." Substack, July 11, 2026.
resources.author: Institute for Critical Study of Antizionism (ICSA)

resources.title: By Ernest Sternberg: "Dog-Rape and Organ Harvesting: The Logic of Humanitarian Blood Libel"
resources.description: The author argues that claims of dog-rape and organ harvesting against Israel, such as Nicholas Kristof's reliance on Euro-Med Human Rights Monitor, are modern blood libels, and shows the organ-theft claim is medically implausible. He contends that progressive humanitarianism now plays the role that race pseudoscience played in earlier antisemitism, serving as a respectable vehicle for demonizing Zionists.
resources.reference: Institute for Critical Study of Antizionism (ICSA). "By Ernest Sternberg: "Dog-Rape and Organ Harvesting: The Logic of Humanitarian Blood Libel"." Substack, May 31, 2026.
resources.author: Institute for Critical Study of Antizionism (ICSA)

resources.title: By Simon Lucas, "Academic antizionism as secularized religious dogma"
resources.description: The author argues that contemporary academic antizionism functions as a secularized religious dogma, with mythic narratives, replacement theology, ritual confession, and heresy policing replacing empirical rigor and open inquiry. He contends this undermines the university's commitment to truth-seeking and suppresses dissent through publishing gatekeeping and social pressure.
resources.reference: Institute for Critical Study of Antizionism (ICSA). "By Simon Lucas, "Academic antizionism as secularized religious dogma"." Substack, May 11, 2026.
resources.author: Institute for Critical Study of Antizionism (ICSA)

resources.title: By Russell Shalev: "A Bespoke Slur: Why 'Ethnocracy' is a Pseudo-Academic Weapon Against Israel"
resources.description: The author argues that 'ethnocracy' is a term coined specifically to delegitimize Israel and is applied selectively, since democracies like Greece and Estonia have comparable ethnic and diaspora ties. He also disputes claims of discriminatory Israeli land law and argues a Palestinian state would itself be an ethnostate.
resources.reference: Institute for Critical Study of Antizionism (ICSA). "By Russell Shalev: "A Bespoke Slur: Why 'Ethnocracy' is a Pseudo-Academic Weapon Against Israel"." Substack, May 2, 2026.
resources.author: Institute for Critical Study of Antizionism (ICSA)

resources.title: By Allen Zeesman: How Antisemitism Adapts to the Moral Language of Each Age
resources.description: The author, drawing on Jonathan Sacks, argues that antisemitism persists by adapting to the dominant moral language of each era (religious, national, racial, and now liberal discourse centered on power and justice). In the contemporary liberal age, he contends, it often takes the form of antizionism, in which Israel is classed as 'powerful' and judged asymmetrically.
resources.reference: Institute for Critical Study of Antizionism (ICSA). "By Allen Zeesman: How Antisemitism Adapts to the Moral Language of Each Age." Substack, May 2, 2026.
resources.author: Institute for Critical Study of Antizionism (ICSA)

resources.title: By Erez Levin, "The Linguistic Shell Game"
resources.description: The author argues that 'antisemitism' has been diluted by overuse, while antizionism, which he says advocates dismantling Israel, has been sanitized as academic critique. He proposes a 'hierarchy of harm' that separates tropes and legitimate policy critique from eliminationist Jew-hatred and antizionism, and urges reserving the strongest condemnation for the latter.
resources.reference: Institute for Critical Study of Antizionism (ICSA). "By Erez Levin, "The Linguistic Shell Game"." Substack, April 26, 2026.
resources.author: Institute for Critical Study of Antizionism (ICSA)

resources.title: By Marcia Kupfer, "'Palestine'" as a geographic label in popular and academic histories"
resources.description: The author argues that after October 7, Western antizionist discourse turned 'Palestine' into both a totalizing moral cause and a trivialized meme, using 'context' and decolonization frames to negate Israeli victimhood. She contends this reproduces older Christian anti-Jewish supersessionist tropes, such as the 'Palestinian Jesus,' and conflates antizionism with exclusion of Jews in practice.
resources.reference: Institute for Critical Study of Antizionism (ICSA). "By Marcia Kupfer, "'Palestine'" as a geographic label in popular and academic histories"." Substack, March 27, 2026.

resources.title: By Eric Daniel Buesing, "From Eugenics to Anti-Zionism: Elite Philanthropy and the Structural Marginalization of Jewish Self-Determination"
resources.description: The author argues, using Foucault's genealogical method, that the Ford, Rockefeller, Carnegie, and Mellon foundations have shifted from funding eugenics and immigration restriction aimed at Jews to funding BDS groups and decolonial academic pipelines that delegitimize Israel. The paper contends that the institutional effect on Jewish self-determination has stayed the same even as the ideological vocabulary changed.
resources.reference: Institute for Critical Study of Antizionism (ICSA). "By Eric Daniel Buesing, "From Eugenics to Anti-Zionism: Elite Philanthropy and the Structural Marginalization of Jewish Self-Determination"." Substack, March 27, 2026.

resources.title: By Robert Goldberg, "Amalek: The Archetypal Anti-Zionist Jew"
resources.description: The author argues that Amalek functions as a transhistorical archetype for the antizionist Jew, with the Haggadah's Wicked Son as his internal form and modern Jewish antizionists as contemporary incarnations. He contends such positions threaten Jewish continuity and calls for an unapologetic affirmation of Zionism as integral to Jewish destiny.
resources.reference: Institute for Critical Study of Antizionism (ICSA). "By Robert Goldberg, "Amalek: The Archetypal Anti-Zionist Jew"." Substack, March 23, 2026.
resources.author: Institute for Critical Study of Antizionism (ICSA)

resources.title: By Kenneth Levin, "Varieties of Jewish Antizionism"
resources.description: Kenneth Levin argues that Jewish antizionism, from JVP and 'as-a-Jew' critics to institutions embracing BLM and DEI, is a recurring maladaptive response of besieged minorities seeking acceptance by adopting their haters' indictments. He traces this pattern from Enlightenment-era reform through the Pittsburgh Platform and Warburg and Magnes to today, and contends that blaming Israeli policy for antisemitism misdiagnoses the threat to American Jews.
resources.reference: Institute for Critical Study of Antizionism (ICSA). "By Kenneth Levin, "Varieties of Jewish Antizionism"." Substack, March 22, 2026.
resources.author: Institute for Critical Study of Antizionism (ICSA)

resources.title: The Foundational Book Project Launches!
resources.description: The author announces a four-volume edited encyclopedia on antizionism and solicits chapter proposals, with a paid contribution offer. He lays out the volume structure and argues that antizionism should be studied in its own right, as a century-long global campaign running from Nazi and Soviet sources through Islamist and Western progressive actors.
resources.reference: Institute for Critical Study of Antizionism (ICSA). "The Foundational Book Project Launches!." Substack, March 19, 2026.
resources.author: Institute for Critical Study of Antizionism (ICSA)

resources.title: Gregg Rosenberg, "A Wolfe in Sheep’s Clothing: A Critique of Israeli ‘Settler-Colonialism’"
resources.description: Philosopher Gregg Rosenberg argues that Patrick Wolfe's settler-colonial paradigm, as applied to Israel by scholars like Rashid Khalidi, has become an unfalsifiable moral technology rather than a scholarly tool. He contends the model fails on the 'foreign settler' and 'metropole' requirements and that Zionism is better understood as a national liberation movement of an indigenous, stateless people.
resources.reference: Institute for Critical Study of Antizionism (ICSA). "Gregg Rosenberg, "A Wolfe in Sheep’s Clothing: A Critique of Israeli ‘Settler-Colonialism’"." Substack, March 13, 2026.
resources.author: Institute for Critical Study of Antizionism (ICSA)

resources.title: (1) Review of Jesella, "Feminist Antisemitism," and (2) "Feminism, Antisemitism and Authoritarianism on the Left," by Daniel Burston
resources.description: The author shares Daniel Burston's review of Kara Jesella's forthcoming book on feminist antisemitism, which traces how feminism's identity-based theories came to cast Jews and Israel as oppressors, plus the abstract and opening of his essay on antizionism, authoritarianism, and denial of October 7 sexual violence on the Left. Burston argues that settler-colonial framings of Israel ignore historical facts and that Left authoritarianism shares dogmatism, conspiracy thinking, and antisemitism with its Right-wing counterpart.

resources.title: "The Great Lethal Projection: Antizionism’s Debt to the Protocols," by Richard Landes
resources.description: The author argues that the Protocols of the Elders of Zion is best read as a gentile projection of the dominating imperative onto Jews, which the Bolsheviks and Nazis used to justify their own domination and genocide. He suggests antizionism, especially accusing Israel of genocide, continues this pattern, and asks whether antizionist progressives fear their Islamist allies or unconsciously share those desires.

resources.title: A Taxonomy of Antizionism by Cary Nelson
resources.description: Cary Nelson argues that antizionism should become a formal academic field and proposes a preliminary 21-item taxonomy covering its key claims, conspiracy theories, adapted antisemitic tropes, academic and institutional entrenchment, and social structures. He contends that since October 7th antizionism and antisemitism have fused and that faculty have been central in spreading antizionist arguments.

resources.title: Time for the Critical Study of Antizionism
resources.description: The author announces the launch of the Institute for the Critical Study of Antizionism, with webinars, a planned book and conference, and scholar recruitment. He supplements this with three pieces arguing that antizionism is a distinct, libel-driven hate ideology that took root in academia and requires its own critical study and response, separate from the label of antisemitism.

resources.author: Andrew Pessin

resources.title: Protocols of the Elders of Anti-Zionism
resources.description: The author proposes a four-part project: an essay framing a century-long global conspiracy against Zionism (an inversion of the Protocols), a conference, an edited book, and an Institute for the Critical Study of Antizionism modeled as a counter to the Institute for the Critical Study of Zionism. He argues antizionism has its own history, logic, and methods that merit scholarly study and seeks collaborators and institutional support.
resources.reference: Andrew Pessin. "Protocols of the Elders of Anti-Zionism." Substack, June 16, 2025.
resources.author: Andrew Pessin

resources.title: Protocols of the Elders of Anti-Zion
resources.description: The author inverts the Protocols of the Elders of Zion, arguing that a real century-long conspiracy exists against the Jews, built by Russian antisemites, the Nazis, the Mufti, and especially Soviet propaganda and 'Zionology' scholarship. He cites Tabarovsky and Pacepa to claim the Soviets created the PLO, spread the Protocols in Arabic, and recast the Arab-Israeli conflict as colonizer versus indigenous.
resources.reference: Andrew Pessin. "Protocols of the Elders of Anti-Zion." Substack, May 3, 2025.
resources.author: Andrew Pessin

resources.title: Protocols of the Elders of Anti-Zion, Part I
resources.description: The author argues that the Protocols of the Elders of Zion inspired an actual century-long conspiracy against Jews, running from Nazi propaganda and scholarship through Soviet anti-Zionist campaigns and the creation of the PLO to today's progressive anti-Zionism. Drawing on Izabella Tabarovsky's work and Ion Pacepa's testimony, he contends that Soviet propaganda deliberately reframed the Arab-Israeli conflict as colonizer versus indigenous people.
resources.reference: Andrew Pessin. "Protocols of the Elders of Anti-Zion, Part I." Substack, March 28, 2025.
resources.author: Andrew Pessin

resources.title: “Anti-Zionism is Antisemitism,” on Campus
resources.description: The author argues that, while not every antizionist is an antisemite, antizionism in its actual manifestations, especially on North American campuses, is generally a species of antisemitism. He builds the case from the entanglement of Zionism with Jewish identity, antisemites' attraction to antizionism, shared tropes, and the rise in anti-Jewish incidents since October 7th.
resources.reference: Andrew Pessin. "“Anti-Zionism is Antisemitism,” on Campus." Substack, Feb. 21, 2025.
resources.author: Andrew Pessin

resources.title: Hate at a Liberal Arts College and the People Who Do Not Speak
resources.description: The author argues that Connecticut College's thirteen-lecture series against Israel is one-sided propaganda that dehumanizes Jews, obsessively singles out Israel, and relies on the genocide libel. He disputes the genocide claim with arguments from Gaza casualty and bombing data, and calls on the silent faculty and administration to speak out.
resources.reference: Andrew Pessin. "Hate at a Liberal Arts College and the People Who Do Not Speak." Substack, Feb. 18, 2025.
resources.author: Andrew Pessin

resources.title: "Anti-Zionism is Antisemitism," On Campus, Fourth (Final) Installment
resources.description: The author argues that common campus anti-Zionist slogans, genocide allegations, BDS, and the 'Drop Hillel' campaign are antisemitic in their context, motivations, and consequences. He also offers indicators for when ostensibly legitimate criticism of Israel crosses into antisemitism, such as activism that is far more anti-Israel than pro-Palestinian.
resources.reference: Andrew Pessin. ""Anti-Zionism is Antisemitism," On Campus, Fourth (Final) Installment." Substack, Jan. 26, 2025.
resources.author: Andrew Pessin

resources.title: "Anti-Zionism is Antisemitism," On Campus, Third Installment
resources.description: The author rebuts three arguments Mehdi Hasan made in a Munk debate against the resolution that anti-Zionism is antisemitism, contending that Zionism is deeply embedded in Jewish identity and history. He argues that Jewish anti-Zionists, including Satmar and Neturei Karta, do not refute the claim, citing historical examples of Jews who served antisemitic movements and distinguishing antisemitism in intent from antisemitism in effect.
resources.reference: Andrew Pessin. ""Anti-Zionism is Antisemitism," On Campus, Third Installment." Substack, Jan. 4, 2025.
resources.author: Andrew Pessin

resources.title: "Anti-Zionism is Antisemitism," On Campus, Second Installment
resources.description: The author argues that antizionism is antisemitic because it rests on "epistemic antisemitism", a readiness to believe false allegations against Jews/Israel, and because its consequences and methods (BDS, calls to dismantle Israel, campus silencing, celebration of October 7) harm Jews. He criticizes the Jerusalem and Nexus definitions for ignoring context and begins arguing that campus antizionism depends on treating Israel's 1948 founding as illegitimate.
resources.reference: Andrew Pessin. ""Anti-Zionism is Antisemitism," On Campus, Second Installment." Substack, Dec. 26, 2024.
resources.author: Andrew Pessin

resources.title: "Anti-Zionism is Antisemitism," On Campus
resources.description: The author argues that, despite exceptions, anti-Zionism is in general a species of antisemitism, given its opposition to a project central to most Jews' identity, its appeal to classic antisemites, and its recycling of traditional antisemitic tropes. He builds the case through definitions (favoring Elder of Ziyon's) and campus examples, presenting this as the first section of a longer essay.
resources.reference: Andrew Pessin. ""Anti-Zionism is Antisemitism," On Campus." Substack, Dec. 20, 2024.
resources.author: Andrew Pessin

resources.title: Even If (Most Of) What Detractors Say About The Founding Of Israel Were True …
resources.description: The author argues that campus reactions to October 7 rest on the premise that Israel's 1948 founding was unjust. He contends that even if most of that premise were granted, it would not justify the movement to undo Israel. His case is that children are a moral fresh start, that demanding rectification of historical wrongs from later generations is itself unjust, and that such claims run in all directions.
resources.reference: Andrew Pessin. "Even If (Most Of) What Detractors Say About The Founding Of Israel Were True …." Substack, Sept. 6, 2024.
resources.author: Andrew Pessin

resources.title: The Indelible Stain of Antisemitism: The Failure of ‘Jew-Washing’
resources.description: The author argues that anti-Israel positions meeting the '3-D' test cannot be exonerated by pointing to 'Social Justice Jews' who ground their anti-Israelism in universal Jewish ethics, since they sidestep the particularist side of Judaism and reject for Jews the rights granted to other peoples. He concludes that targeting Zionist Jews amounts to a 'new antisemitism' that Judea Pearl has called 'Zionophobia.'
resources.reference: Andrew Pessin. "The Indelible Stain of Antisemitism: The Failure of ‘Jew-Washing’." Substack, May 28, 2024.
resources.author: Andrew Pessin

resources.title: What They Talk About When They Talk About Israel
resources.description: The author argues that the distinction between antizionism and antisemitism rarely exists in practice, since talk about Israel, the Jewish state, almost always connotes Jews. He supports this with historical examples, campus incidents, boycott logic, and quotations from antizionists, and contends that the real debate concerns what is said about Israel.
resources.reference: Andrew Pessin. "What They Talk About When They Talk About Israel." Substack, Feb. 26, 2024.
resources.author: Andrew Pessin

resources.title: Even If (Most Of) What Detractors Say About The Founding Of Israel Were True ... (Part 1 of 2)
resources.description: The author argues that campus celebration of October 7 rests on the premise that Israel's 1948 founding was an injustice, and that BDS and progressivism have dehumanized Jews. Even granting the detractors' narrative, he argues, descendants cannot justly be held responsible or entitled for ancestral injustices, so demands to undo Israel remain morally objectionable.
